newsitem.title: USA: Major players in O.J. Simpson civil trial.
newsitem.headline: Major players in O.J. Simpson civil trial.

text.p: Following are the major players in the wrongful death lawsuit brought against O.J. Simpson by the families of murder victims Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman.
THE DEFENDANT
-- O.J. Simpson, a former football star who also had careers as a sportscaster, actor and advertising pitchman. He was acquitted on Oct. 3, 1995, in the murders of his ex-wife and her friend.

Since the end of his yearlong criminal trial, Simpson has maintained his innocence in a series of TV interviews and in his own mail-order video, contending he was framed by the Los Angeles Police Department. Despite his efforts to repair his image, polls show that most whites believe he got away with murder while most blacks support the verdict that freed the top black celebrity.
THE JUDGE
-- Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki, a 16-year veteran of the bench who was assigned to handle the Simpson case after defence attorneys removed Judge Alan Haber.

Fujisaki said he would not tolerate a "circus atmosphere" in the civil case; one of his first acts as trial judge was to impose a strict gag order on trial lawyers. He followed that with a ban on cameras and tape recorders from the courtroom.
THE PLAINTIFFS

-- Sharon Rufo, Ronald Goldman's mother, who was divorced from his father, Fred Goldman, in 1974. Fred Goldman was awarded custody of Ron and his sister, Kim; Rufo apparently had limited contact with Ron in the intervening years.
Rufo was the first to sue Simpson, filing her complaint about five weeks after the murders. A resident of St. Louis, Missouri, she was rarely seen at the criminal trial.

-- Fred Goldman and Kim Goldman, Ron's father and sister, who in May 1995 filed suit against Simpson in a separate action from Rufo's. Both attended the criminal trial almost daily and were outspoken in their belief that Simpson committed the murders.

-- The estate of Nicole Brown Simpson, in a lawsuit filed in May 1995, by her father, Louis Brown, acting as executor. Though Nicole's family members -- including her father, her mother, Juditha, and sisters, Denise, Dominique and Tania -- could be called to testify, they are not named as plaintiffs.
Simpson's two children with Nicole, Sydney, 10, and Justin, 8, are the subject of a custody battle between Simpson and the Brown family.
THE ATTORNEYS
-- Simpson is represented by at least five lawyers, led by veteran Santa Monica civil attorney Robert Baker, his son, Phillip, and associate Melissa Bluestein.

Robert Blasier, a Sacramento-based attorney who specialises in DNA evidence who played a role in Simpson's criminal defence, has signed on for the civil trial. Courtroom legend F. Lee Bailey has also discussed joining the team.
In contrast to the headline-grabbing style of lead criminal lawyer Johnnie Cochran and his "dream team," defence attorneys in the civil case have largely shunned the media.

But in pre-trial hearings, the defence attorneys suggested they would stress some of the same themes that jurors heard in the criminal trial, including a contention that police failed to investigate other possible suspects.
-- The Goldmans are represented by Los Angeles attorney Daniel Petrocelli and several associates, including Edward Medvene and Peter Gelblum.
Petrocelli, a New Jersey native who finished first in his class in law school, took the lead in many pre-trial issues and in depositions, earning praise for his thorough style.
-- The estate of Nicole Brown Simpson is represented by New York attorney John Quinlan Kelly and Los Angeles lawyer Natasha Roit.
-- Rufo is represented by Los Angeles attorney Michael Brewer, a Los Angeles attorney who graduated from law school in 1985 and has specialised in civil litigation for his firm.
